name: sidecar_wal_without_shm
description: The workspace includes a stray WAL sidecar without a matching SHM sidecar or coordinated writer state.
source_hint: Represents the stale or missing sidecar family called out in rsei.2.1.
notes: The database file itself is healthy so future tests can isolate how startup reacts to sidecar mismatch.
The WAL payload is intentionally synthetic and small.

sync --status expected status_in_sync until bds-04l.4.3. That encoded the previous storage engine's handling of a stub WAL: it reported one as WalCorrupt, which is in should_attempt_jsonl_recovery's set, so opening the workspace rebuilt the database from JSONL and left it in sync. Real SQLite has no WAL-corrupt result code -- a WAL that does not validate is discarded silently (src/storage/conn.rs) -- so the database opens normally and the schema migration marks its issue dirty, exactly as it does for orphan_shm_sidecar and journal_sidecar_leftover. All three now report an identical posture, and all three expect status_db_newer.
